# Methods : Schema Design Reference

Tables and reference data used by `postgres-core-schema-design`. All facts verified against postgresql.org/docs/17 unless otherwise noted.

## IDENTITY Columns (v10+) : `GENERATED ALWAYS` vs `GENERATED BY DEFAULT`

| Aspect | `GENERATED ALWAYS AS IDENTITY` | `GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY` |
|---|---|---|
| `INSERT` without value | sequence allocates | sequence allocates |
| `INSERT` with explicit value | error 428C9 | accepted, sequence not advanced |
| `INSERT ... OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` | accepted | accepted (no-op : already accepted) |
| `INSERT ... OVERRIDING USER VALUE` | accepted (overrides user, uses sequence) | accepted (overrides user, uses sequence) |
| `UPDATE col = literal` | error : "column ... can only be updated to DEFAULT" | accepted |
| `UPDATE col = DEFAULT` | accepted (sequence allocates) | accepted (sequence allocates) |
| Use case | Surrogate key, app should never know id | Distributed-id, migration loads, hybrid |
| Sequence visibility | Owned by column, dropped on column drop | Owned by column, dropped on column drop |

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createtable.html (Identity Columns), postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-insert.html (`overriding_clause`).

## SERIAL vs IDENTITY (why IDENTITY won) :

| Property | `serial` (v9.6 and back-compat) | `GENERATED ... AS IDENTITY` (v10+) |
|---|---|---|
| Column type | `integer` (max ~2.1B) | `integer` / `bigint` (caller picks) |
| Sequence ownership | Created and OWNED BY column, but not formally part of the column constraint | Strictly owned by the identity ; cannot be detached |
| GRANT semantics | INSERT-grantee on the table needs separate USAGE on the sequence | Implicit : INSERT grant covers identity allocation |
| `ALTER COLUMN TYPE` | Breaks the implicit sequence dependency | Sequence migrates with the column |
| `pg_dump --schema-only` output | Multiple statements (CREATE SEQUENCE, ALTER OWNED BY, ALTER COLUMN DEFAULT) | One `GENERATED AS IDENTITY` clause |
| SQL standard | PostgreSQL-only | ANSI SQL-2003 |
| INSERT override | Always allowed (the DEFAULT is just `nextval(...)`) | Requires `OVERRIDING SYSTEM VALUE` (ALWAYS) |

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/datatype-numeric.html (Serial Types), postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createtable.html (Identity Columns).

## `search_path` Resolution Levels (precedence : right column wins) :

| Level | Where set | Survives reconnect? | Read via |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cluster | `postgresql.conf : search_path = '...'` | Yes | `SHOW search_path` (without overrides) |
| Database | `ALTER DATABASE x SET search_path = ...` | Yes | `SELECT datconfig FROM pg_database WHERE datname=...` |
| Role | `ALTER ROLE r SET search_path = ...` | Yes | `SELECT rolconfig FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname=...` |
| Role-in-database | `ALTER ROLE r IN DATABASE x SET search_path = ...` | Yes | `pg_db_role_setting` system catalog |
| Session | `SET search_path = ...` | No | `SHOW search_path` (current session) |
| Transaction | `SET LOCAL search_path = ...` | No (resets at COMMIT/ROLLBACK) | `SHOW search_path` inside the transaction |
| Function | `CREATE FUNCTION ... SET search_path = ...` | No (per-call) | `\df+ funcname` proconfig column |

The effective `search_path` at any moment is the most-specific override : function > transaction > session > role-in-database > role > database > cluster default.

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/config-setting.html, postgresql.org/docs/17/runtime-config-client.html (`search_path`).

## Default `search_path` Behavior :

Default value (post-initdb) : `"$user", public`.

| Element | Meaning | If missing |
|---|---|---|
| `"$user"` | A schema whose name matches `current_user` | Silently skipped : no error |
| `public` | The `public` schema | Silently skipped : no error |
| `pg_catalog` | Always searched FIRST, implicitly, regardless of `search_path` | Cannot be removed (always implicit) |
| `pg_temp` | The per-session temporary schema, searched FIRST when present unless pinned later | Created on first temp-table creation |

To force `pg_temp` to be searched LAST (CRITICAL for SECURITY DEFINER) : list it explicitly at the end of `search_path`. Anything before it overrides the implicit-first behavior.

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-schemas.html (Schema Search Path), postgresql.org/docs/17/runtime-config-client.html.

## SCHEMA Privileges (GRANT matrix) :

| Privilege | Effect | When required |
|---|---|---|
| `USAGE` | Allows referencing objects inside the schema (without it, role cannot SELECT even with table-level SELECT) | Every consumer role |
| `CREATE` | Allows creating objects (tables, views, sequences, types, functions) in the schema | Schema owner OR explicitly granted |

Default privileges per schema after `CREATE SCHEMA x` (v15+ fresh database) :

| Role | USAGE on `x` | CREATE on `x` |
|---|---|---|
| Schema owner | yes (implicit) | yes (implicit) |
| `PUBLIC` | no | no |

Default privileges on `public` schema :

| PostgreSQL version | `PUBLIC` USAGE on public | `PUBLIC` CREATE on public |
|---|---|---|
| v14 and earlier | yes | yes (open by default — CVE-2018-1058 vector) |
| v15+ fresh database | yes | no (revoked at initdb time) |
| v15+ database upgraded in place from v14 | yes | yes (carries old grant) |

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-schemas.html (Public Schema), postgresql.org/docs/15/release-15.html.

## SECURITY DEFINER Function : Required Clauses

A `SECURITY DEFINER` function MUST include all of these in its `CREATE FUNCTION` statement to be considered safe :

1. `SECURITY DEFINER` (the directive itself).
2. `SET search_path = pg_catalog, <trusted_schemas>, pg_temp` (pin resolution chain, with `pg_temp` LAST).
3. Schema-qualify all object references inside the body (`admin.pwds`, not bare `pwds`) : defense-in-depth.
4. Restrict execute privileges after creation : `REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION ... FROM PUBLIC ; GRANT EXECUTE TO <intended_role>`.
5. Run the `REVOKE` + `GRANT` atomically in the same transaction as `CREATE FUNCTION` so there is no window where the function exists with PUBLIC execute.

Optional but recommended :

6. `LEAKPROOF` only when the function's exception messages cannot reveal input data (very rare ; default is safer).
7. `STABLE` or `IMMUTABLE` if the function is read-only, so the planner can optimize.

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-createfunction.html (Writing SECURITY DEFINER Functions Safely).

## Naming Conventions (project-wide constants)

| Object | Convention | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Schema | snake_case singular | `auth`, `app`, `etl_staging` |
| Table | snake_case (pick singular OR plural project-wide) | `customer` OR `customers`, never both |
| Column | snake_case | `customer_id`, `created_at`, `is_active` |
| Primary key | `id` (preferred for `USING(id)` joins) OR `<entity>_id` (preferred for self-describing joins) | `id` or `customer_id` |
| Foreign key column | `<referenced_entity>_id` | `customer_id`, `order_id` |
| Junction table | `<a>_<b>` alphabetical | `customer_tag` (not `tag_customer`) |
| Index | `<table>_<column(s)>_<type>_idx` | `customer_email_btree_idx`, `order_jsonb_data_gin_idx` |
| Unique constraint | `<table>_<column(s)>_uq` | `customer_email_uq` |
| Check constraint | `<table>_<column>_chk` | `order_status_chk` |
| Foreign key constraint | `<table>_<column>_fk` | `order_customer_id_fk` |
| Sequence (auto) | `<table>_<column>_seq` (PostgreSQL default) | `customer_id_seq` |
| Function | snake_case verb_noun | `compute_invoice_total`, `check_password` |
| Trigger | `<table>_<action>_<timing>_trg` | `audit_log_insert_after_trg` |

Reserved-word list (NEVER use as identifier) : `user`, `order`, `table`, `column`, `index`, `constraint`, `select`, `from`, `where`, `group`, `having`, `limit`, `offset`, `case`, `when`, `then`, `else`, `end`, `null`, `true`, `false`, `default`, `primary`, `references`, `unique`, `check`, `cast`, `desc`, `asc`. The full list is at postgresql.org/docs/17/sql-keywords-appendix.html.

## Multi-Tenant Decision Reference :

| Approach | Tenants | DDL changes | Cross-tenant query | Backup granularity | Isolation strength |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| schema-per-tenant | < 50 | N-pass per change | `SELECT FROM t1.orders UNION ALL t2.orders ...` | per-schema via `pg_dump --schema` | Strong (GRANT-level) |
| RLS in shared schema | 50 - 10,000 | 1-pass | Privileged role with BYPASSRLS or no policy | Database-wide only | Medium (policy correctness) |
| database-per-tenant | > 10,000 OR regulated | Per-tenant migration scripts (orchestrated) | None without FDW | Per-database | Strongest (no shared catalog) |

Combinations are legitimate : a database-per-tenant deployment can ALSO use schema-per-module within each tenant. RLS can be added inside a schema-per-tenant deployment for finer-grained per-row checks.

Source : postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-rowsecurity.html, postgresql.org/docs/17/ddl-schemas.html, real-world deployments documented at supabase.com/docs/guides/database/postgres/row-level-security (verified pattern).

## Detection Queries :

### `serial` columns still in the database (candidates for IDENTITY migration) :

```sql
SELECT n.nspname AS schema,
       c.relname AS table,
       a.attname AS column,
       pg_get_serial_sequence(n.nspname || '.' || c.relname, a.attname) AS seq
FROM pg_attribute a
  JOIN pg_class c ON a.attrelid = c.oid
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON c.relnamespace = n.oid
WHERE c.relkind = 'r'
  AND a.attnum > 0
  AND NOT a.attisdropped
  AND pg_get_serial_sequence(n.nspname || '.' || c.relname, a.attname) IS NOT NULL
  AND NOT a.attidentity IN ('a','d');
```

### `public` schema is writable by `PUBLIC` :

```sql
SELECT has_schema_privilege('public', 'public', 'CREATE') AS public_can_create;
-- t means CVE-2018-1058 vector is open. Fix : REVOKE CREATE ON SCHEMA public FROM PUBLIC;
```

### `SECURITY DEFINER` functions without pinned `search_path` :

```sql
SELECT n.nspname || '.' || p.proname AS function,
       p.prosecdef AS security_definer,
       p.proconfig AS settings
FROM pg_proc p
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON p.pronamespace = n.oid
WHERE p.prosecdef
  AND (p.proconfig IS NULL
       OR NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1 FROM unnest(p.proconfig) AS cfg
         WHERE cfg LIKE 'search_path=%'
       ));
```

### Quoted-identifier inventory (any mixed-case or special-char names) :

```sql
SELECT n.nspname, c.relname
FROM pg_class c
  JOIN pg_namespace n ON c.relnamespace = n.oid
WHERE c.relkind IN ('r','v','m','i','S')
  AND (c.relname ~ '[A-Z]'
       OR c.relname ~ '[^a-z0-9_]'
       OR quote_ident(c.relname) <> c.relname);
```

Source for detection patterns : postgresql.org/docs/17/catalogs.html (pg_attribute, pg_proc, pg_namespace), postgresql.org/docs/17/functions-info.html (`has_schema_privilege`).
